name: manymotions-ai-video-editor
description: Edit the video projects in your ManyMotions account from ChatGPT: rearrange and remove clips, place clips from the project library, set transitions, add subtitles from text and export the finished MP4.

interface.longDescription:
Edit the video projects in your ManyMotions account by asking ChatGPT.

Ask for the timeline of a project and ChatGPT lists every clip in playback order with its length. Then edit it in plain words: move a clip to the start, remove a take, place another clip from the project library, add a fade or a slide between two clips, or add subtitles by pasting SRT or VTT text or by giving ChatGPT the lines and their timing. When the cut is ready, ask for the export: ManyMotions renders the timeline into one MP4 with the transitions, the audio and the burned-in subtitles, and ChatGPT returns the link.

For creators and marketers who keep their clips in ManyMotions and want to assemble the final cut without opening the editor.

Limitations: the plugin edits existing projects in your signed-in ManyMotions account. It does not generate new clips, images, voices or music, does not upload or import files, does not create projects and does not trim clips or change their speed or volume; for those, use the editor on manymotions.com.

ManyMotions is the platform formerly known as ClipWave.
capabilities: Read and rearrange a video timeline
defaultPrompt: Show me the timeline of my Weekend Reel project
In Weekend Reel, move the last clip to the start and add a fade between the first two clips
Export my Weekend Reel project as an MP4

positive.prompt: Show me the timeline of my Weekend Reel project in ManyMotions.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the "Weekend Reel" project and lists the clips of its main video in playback order (for example Travel clip, Workout clip, Comedy clip) with their durations and the total length of about 41 seconds. Nothing is changed.

positive.prompt: In my Weekend Reel project, move the last clip to the beginning of the video.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the timeline, moves the last clip on the video track to position 1 and reports the new order of the clips.

positive.prompt: In Weekend Reel, add a half-second fade between the first and the second clip.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the timeline and sets a "fade" transition of 0.5 seconds on the first clip, so it blends into the second one on export.

positive.prompt: Add two subtitles to my Weekend Reel video: "Our weekend, in one minute" from 0 to 3 seconds and "First stop: the coast" from 3 to 6 seconds.
positive.expected_behavior: Adds the 2 captions to the main video of "Weekend Reel" (replacing any previous ones) and confirms that they are burned in when the video is exported.

positive.prompt: Export my Weekend Reel project as an MP4 and give me the download link.
positive.expected_behavior: Renders the timeline of "Weekend Reel" into one vertical MP4 (usually within one or two minutes) and returns its absolute link with the duration. No credits are used.

negative.prompt: Create a new 10-second video of a sunset over the ocean.
What is the best free desktop video editing software for beginners?
Summarize the main differences between the H.264 and H.265 video codecs.

review.commerce_description: The plugin does not sell products or process payments. It edits projects in the user's existing ManyMotions account; editing and exporting do not use credits.

publication.release_notes: Resubmission with no functional changes: read a project timeline, rearrange clips, add transitions and subtitles, and export the MP4 from the linked ManyMotions account.
